rows.drawdown: The investor commits an amount up front. The manager asks for it in pieces ("calls") as it finds investments, usually over the first several years.
rows.evergreen: No calls. The whole amount is invested when the subscription is accepted; BXPE takes fully funded subscriptions monthly.

sources.name: PIMCO, Understanding alternatives: speak the language

rows.drawdown: Gradually. Until it's called, the committed money sits wherever the investor keeps it, and early investments are being sold and paid back before the last calls come in.
rows.evergreen: All at once, into a portfolio that already exists. Part of the fund may be held in cash or easier-to-sell assets to pay redemptions.

sources.name: PIMCO, Understanding alternatives: speak the language

rows.drawdown: Common. Fees and costs come before gains, so reported returns are often negative in the first years and turn up later as investments are sold.
rows.evergreen: Less pronounced at the fund level, since a new investor buys into seasoned holdings. Fees are charged on the fund's value from the first month.

sources.name: PIMCO, Understanding alternatives: speak the language

rows.drawdown: Generally none until investments are sold; money comes back as the fund exits holdings. Selling a stake early means finding a buyer on the secondary market, often at a discount.
rows.evergreen: Periodic repurchases up to a limit. BXPE offers up to 3% of units a quarter across the fund, with a 5% deduction on units held under two years; the manager can change or suspend it.
rows.evergreenShort: Buybacks each quarter, up to a limit

rows.drawdown: Commonly a management fee charged on committed capital during the investment period, and carried interest (often 20%) on profits above a preferred return; terms vary by fund.
rows.evergreen: BXPE: 1.25% a year of net asset value, plus 12.5% of total return once it clears a 5% annual hurdle, with a full catch-up and a high-water mark. Share classes add servicing fees of up to 0.85% a year.

sources.name: PIMCO, Understanding alternatives: speak the language

rows.drawdownShort: Fee on committed money, plus carry
rows.evergreenShort: Fee on NAV, plus 12.5% over a 5% hurdle

rows.drawdown: Private funds generally aren't registered offerings; investors get reports set by the fund's agreement.
rows.evergreen: BXPE files 10-Q and 10-K reports with the SEC and publishes a net asset value each month.
rows.evergreenShort: SEC filings and a monthly NAV

rows.drawdown: Subscription documents up front, then a cash transfer for each capital call over several years; partnership tax forms (Schedule K-1).
rows.evergreen: One subscription, then periodic statements. BXPE and BX Infra send tax information on Schedule K-1s or their equivalent.

sources.name: BXPE Form 10-K, year ended December 31, 2025
sources.page: Item 1A: Risk Factors, General Tax Considerations

sources.name: Tax Lens: how BXPE is taxed

rows.drawdown: A set term, commonly around ten years, often with extensions.
rows.evergreen: No end date. BXPE describes itself as perpetual-life, established for an indefinite period.

sources.name: PIMCO, Understanding alternatives: speak the language

drawdown: Investors who can keep cash or bonds ready for calls over several years, and want each fund's money returned as its investments are sold.
Portfolios that want to choose vintage years and managers one fund at a time.
Holders comfortable with a fixed, long lock-up in exchange for no redemption queue.
evergreen: Investors who want the full amount working from day one, without managing future calls.
Portfolios that value some periodic liquidity, accepting it is limited and can be prorated or suspended.
Holders who prefer one ongoing position over a series of fund vintages.
